items.title: The things you can now do directly in the browser
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​768 — November 25, 2026 | Read on the web Things You Can Do With a Browser in 2027 — Luigi returns with a sequel to the popular browser-2020 list, highlighting some of the lesser-known things browsers can do today, including HTML-in-Canvas, the model > element, HDR, on-device AI, hardware APIs, and more. Each feature is quickly explained alongside a browser support table. Luigi De Rosa Agents Didn’t Clear Your Plate. They Dumped Reviews on It — Your agents write PRs in minutes, then eat your afternoon in review. When did ‘saving time’ start to mean babysitting agents’ work? Meticulous verifies every UI change, with no developer effort. Devs at Dropbox & ElevenLabs have their afternoons back. You can too. Meticulous sponsor Nudeps: npm Imports in the Browser — A new tool from Lea Verou and Dmitry Sharabin that lets you npm install packages and import them by name directly within the browser, no bundler required . It builds upon thinking outlined in Lea's ' Web dependencies are broken ' article from earlier this year. Lea Verou When Everything Has Changed, What Do We Do Next? — A post that takes stock of the year we've had, where the AI bubble has undoubtedly reshaped the industry. Andy argues that developers are more than "code slingers," and makes the case for investing in people, building by hand, and keeping independent publishing alive. Andy Bell ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🦊 Firefox 161 is out and adds support for the CSS random() function (more on that later), plus Compression Dictionary Transport . 🐞 The Ladybird browser (an effort to build a new browser engine from scratch ) is now in alpha , available for macOS and Linux. You can download it here . ⚙️ Simon Willison has been trying the above Ladybird alpha and shares his initial thoughts here , calling it an " astonishingly ambitious project ". 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials Why There Are Still No Non-WebKit Browsers on iOS — Mozilla says that, three years on, the EU's DMA (along with Japan's newer rules) has ultimately failed to open up iOS to any non-WebKit browser engines. Mozilla 💡 After an open letter from Mozilla, Shopify and others, the European Commission says it's in talks with Apple , and Chrome's team has backed Mozilla's stance too. Understanding CSS random() — As mentioned above, Firefox 161 has joined Chrome and Safari in supporting random() . Here, Mat uses it to give his sidenotes a hand-placed 'jauntiness'. Mat Marquis Foxit Compares 10 HTML to PDF APIs — Rendering engines, CSS and JavaScript handling, headers and footers, and how each API bills a render. Foxit sponsor Has the Web Stopped Getting Heavier? — The pace at which web pages get heavier is levelling off, as HTTP Archive data shows growth has slowed to a crawl, with the median mobile page adding just 7KB of JavaScript in the past year. Sander van Surksum Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality — CSS Grid really changed what was possible for page layouts, but Andy notes that designers still lean heavily on the twelve-column pattern. So he explores some more ambitious layout options that can be easily achieved today. Andy Clarke Playing with CSS Layers — A fun tinkering post from Kitty, experimenting with CSS layers on their personal site just for the joy of it. Kitty Giraudel The Compacting Sidebar Blues — What should an app's sidebar do on a screen that's too short for it? Chris explains why a scroll-state() query loops infinitely here, and what works better instead. Chris Coyier AI Sped Up The Build: How Can Accessibility Testing Keep Up? Andrew Chung A New Set of HTML Insertion and Streaming APIs Amit Merchant Creating Diagrams and Graphs Using Modern CSS Temani Afif 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources Button Sounds: Tactile SFX for Your UI — Josh has pulled together a free collection of 50+ professionally recorded multi-sampled clicks and toggles. Many have the charming thunks and clunks of your favorite keyboard. Distributed as an NPM package with optional React bindings. Josh W. Comeau Your Chart Isn’t Slow. Its Query Is — TimescaleDB extends Postgres so dashboards stay fast as data grows. $1000 credit on Tiger Cloud . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor Alloy CSS: One Stylesheet for the HTML Your Server Renders — A free kit of dialogs, menus, drawers, tabs and toast notifications that all work with JavaScript turned off. Fandy Pradana 🤖 wllama 4.0: Run llama.cpp Models in the Browser — These WebAssembly bindings for llama.cpp let you run GGUF models directly in-browser. v4 doubles inference speed, and models of any size now load, with WebGPU helping out (where available). Try the demos here. Xuan-Son Nguyen ⏱️ 5.5: Format Timestamps as a Localized Relative Time — Supply this web component with a standard date/time and it'll render "2 days ago" , say. GitHub uses this on its repo and code views. GitHub 'CodePen Commander' Brings Pens into Your Local Editor — If you use CodePen Pro, Bramus has built a CLI tool that brings git -style clone/push workflows to CodePen 2.0, along with batch syncing, a local dev server, and one-command deploys. Bramus Van Damme Intro.js: A User-Friendly 'Onboarding Tour' Library — A library for creating step-by-step product tours (as seen during onboarding in SaaS tools, for example). It's AGPL licensed with an optional paid license available too. Afshin Mehrabani Port Menu: A Tiny macOS Menu Bar App To Track Dev Servers Across Projects Eduard Wieandt 📰 Classifieds ⚡ AI agents ignore rules. Nexity’s reviewer agents check every new Next.js + Sanity section against yours: design, schema, GROQ. 🕹️ ...and finally Kirupa’s 404 Arcade — Kirupa turned his 404 page into an awesome arcade with sixteen playable games (riffing on many a classic), complete with synthesized sound, retro stylings, and high-score tables. I mean, why not have some fun if you get lost? Very cool! Kirupa 🖊️ If you prefer something a bit more practical, yet still with some whimsy, Ductus is a neat site that converts your handwriting into a font (OpenType or WOFF2). You can draw the letters right on the page for it to convert.

items.title: Flags SDK now works on Vercel without FLAGS_SECRET
items.summary: With flags@4.5.0 , projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET . That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends. Vercel signs Flags Explorer discovery requests and overrides, and the SDK encrypts flag values shown in the Vercel Toolbar with Vercel’s public key. Existing projects keep using FLAGS_SECRET while the environment variable is set or the secret is passed in code. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull . Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one. If you use a build cache, see the precompute documentation for the required configuration. Learn more in the Flags SDK documentation . Read more

The small multimodal reasoning model is built for agentic coding, tool use, and knowledge work, with text and image inputs and text output. Inkling 2 Mini has 26.4 billion total parameters and 3.4 billion active per token. The model runs its middle layers more than once for every token, which lets it reason further before writing anything down and often reach an answer with fewer reasoning tokens. Like Inkling 2 Small, it is strongest on long-running agentic tasks. The model has a 1M-token context window, and reasoning effort can be set from none through max . Use thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Inkling 2 Mini in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.
items.titleJa: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summaryJa: Shirudoは、Linux系システム上でパッチ適用中の脆弱性を回避するためのオープンソースの実行環境で、eBPFを用いて動作中のサービスを停止させずに一時的な防御層を適用できる。実際の例として、Elasticsearch上でJava4Shellの攻撃をシャールドが入力検証を追加する形で阻止し、サービスを再起動なしに継続させたことが挙げられている。今後は信頼性のある防御を大規模展開できるよう、開発者や研究者、運用担当者が協力して shields のテスト・検証・提供を進める予定である。

items.title: Using Fallbacks for a Robust Front-End
items.summary: It’s important to use fallbacks to build a robust front end, either to quietly and discreetly avoid the error or to communicate it to our users. items.titleJa: Thinking Machines Lab、Macでも動くAIモデル「Inkling 2 Mini」をオープンウェイトで公開 ——中間の12層を3回通るTransformer
